raw_case_text:
A female neonate was born to a 22-year-old healthy primigravida woman at 35 gestational weeks by cesarean section due to fetal distress. Fetal echogenic bowel was determined in an antenatal ultrasound (US) examination at 18 weeks' gestation; however, fetal magnetic resonance-imaging (MRI) revealed no abnormalities. A maternal serologic examination was negative for rubella, Toxoplasma gondii, and cytomegalovirus (CMV) immunoglobulin (Ig)-M. Amniocentesis revealed normal fetal karyotype. Cranial ventriculomegaly was seen using re-performed antenatal US and fetal-MRI (atrial diameter of left ventricle 12.4 mm, right ventricle 13 mm) at 34 gestational weeks. She was admitted to our neonatal intensive care unit because of the ventriculomegaly and prematurity. Her weight was 1870 g (10th percentile), height 44 cm (10-50th percentile), and head circumference 32 cm (50-90th percentile). On physical examination, she appeared well, there was no abnormality except for hepatosplenomegaly (palpable 3 cm below costal-margin). Cranial US performed in the first hour after birth showed mild ventriculomegaly and grade I germinal matrix hemorrhage. Four hours later, widespread petechiae appeared over the entire body of the patient. The blood count [except for thrombocytopenia (19,000/mm3)] and other biochemical and hematologic parameters were within normal values.
The patient's CMV IgM was positive in the blood test. An ophthalmologic assessment revealed bilateral chorioretinitis. Cranial computed tomography (CT) showed ventriculomegaly with no calcifications. The patient failed auditory brainstem response testing. On postnatal day 7, CMV polymerase chain reaction (PCR) was positive in the patient's blood; therefore, she was diagnosed as having a symptomatic congenital CMV infection. The patient's mother's CMV PCR was negative in the blood. At this time, the patient had no respiratory distress symptoms and the initial chest X-ray was normal. Intravenous ganciclovir therapy (12 mg/kg/d, divided into two doses) was started. After two platelet transfusions, platelet counts returned to normal values on the 12th day postnatally.
An abdomen X-ray was performed because of the abdominal distension and feeding intolerance on postnatal day 20. Interestingly, we detected a regular-shaped cystic lesion in the left lower lung zone. This cystic lesion was also seen in a chest X-ray. Afterwards, a thoracic CT confirmed multiple cystic areas in the left lower lung lobe (Fig. 1 a, b). At that time, the patient had no respiratory distress symptoms, additionally, C-reactive protein (CRP) and blood cultures were negative. On the 35th day of ganciclovir therapy, no cystic lung lesions were detected on follow-up chest X-ray. On postnatal day 55, she was discharged with oral valganciclovir therapy (32 mg/kg/d, divided into two doses). We did observed no adverse effects of anti-viral therapy. At the 6th month of therapy, her weight, height, and head-circumference were in normal percentiles. On repeated ophthalmologic examination, macular scars were detected in both eyes; however, reactivation was not observed. Cranial MRI showed bilateral periventricular cysts. Cochlear implantation was planned because of severe sensorineural hearing loss. Informed consent was obtained from her parents.

subjective.chief_complaint: A preterm female neonate born at 35 weeks' gestation presented at birth with prenatally detected bilateral cerebral ventriculomegaly and hepatosplenomegaly, followed 4 hours later by generalized petechiae and severe thrombocytopenia, and on postnatal day 20 by abdominal distension, feeding intolerance, and left lower lobe cystic lung lesions.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Born at 35 weeks' gestation via emergency cesarean section for fetal distress to a 22-year-old primigravida (antenatal history of 18-week fetal echogenic bowel with normal fetal karyotype and negative maternal TORCH/CMV IgM, followed at 34 weeks by bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly on US and fetal MRI), the neonate exhibited hepatosplenomegaly at birth and developed generalized cutaneous petechiae and severe thrombocytopenia (19,000/mm3) at 4 hours of life. While receiving intravenous ganciclovir (started after positive CMV IgM and day 7 blood CMV PCR), she developed abdominal distension and feeding intolerance on postnatal day 20, when abdominal and chest imaging revealed asymptomatic multiple cystic lesions in the left lower lung lobe.
subjective.past_medical_history: Preterm female neonate born at 35 weeks' gestation (birth weight 1,870 g [10th percentile], length 44 cm [10-50th percentile], head circumference 32 cm [50-90th percentile]); prenatal echogenic bowel (18 GW) and bilateral ventriculomegaly (34 GW; left atrium 12.4 mm, right atrium 13 mm).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for generalized petechiae (at 4h of life) and abdominal distension/feeding intolerance (on day 20); negative for respiratory distress throughout hospitalization.

objective.physical_examination: At birth: well-appearing, no respiratory distress, palpable hepatosplenomegaly (3 cm below costal margin), followed 4 hours later by widespread generalized petechiae. Ophthalmologic examination revealed bilateral chorioretinitis (evolving into bilateral inactive macular scars at 6 months). Failed newborn auditory brainstem response (ABR) hearing screen (severe sensorineural hearing loss).
objective.routine_investigations: Birth CBC and biochemistry: severe thrombocytopenia with platelets 19,000/mm3 (normalized by postnatal day 12 after 2 platelet transfusions), normal other hematologic/biochemical parameters. Neonatal blood CMV IgM was positive (maternal blood CMV IgM and CMV PCR were negative). Initial chest X-ray normal; day 20 abdominal and chest X-rays showed a well-defined cystic lesion in the left lower lung zone with negative CRP and blood cultures (completely resolved on day 35 chest X-ray). First-hour cranial ultrasound showed mild bilateral ventriculomegaly and grade I germinal matrix hemorrhage.
objective.advanced_workup: Postnatal day 7 blood CMV PCR was positive. Cranial CT showed bilateral ventriculomegaly without intracranial calcifications; 6-month cranial MRI showed bilateral periventricular cysts. Postnatal day 20 thoracic CT confirmed multiple cystic lesions in the left lower lung lobe.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis of symptomatic congenital cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection complicated by bilateral chorioretinitis, severe sensorineural hearing loss, ventriculomegaly/periventricular cysts, hepatosplenomegaly, severe neonatal thrombocytopenia, and CMV-associated acquired cystic lung lesions of the left lower lobe, confirmed by positive neonatal CMV IgM and postnatal day 7 blood CMV PCR. Treated with 2 platelet transfusions and intravenous ganciclovir (12 mg/kg/day divided BID), which resulted in complete radiographic resolution of the cystic lung lesions by day 35 of therapy, followed at postnatal day 55 discharge by oral valganciclovir maintenance (32 mg/kg/day divided BID). At 6-month follow-up, growth parameters were normal without chorioretinitis reactivation, and cochlear implantation was planned for severe sensorineural hearing loss.
